findings.title: ConsumeMemoShareView test omits the nonexistent-id and zero-limit edges
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate sqlite ConsumeMemoShareView (store/db/sqlite/memo_share.go:184) from `rows == 1` to `rows >= 0`, or drop the `view_count < view_limit` guard for limit 0. TestMemoShareViewLimitConsumption still passes for the cases it covers, but a consume of a deleted or unknown share id would return true, so a revoked link could be reported as claimed. A share with limit 0 is never exercised.
findings.evidence: store/test/memo_share_test.go:214-236 only consumes a limit-2 share and an unlimited share. There is no call with an id that does not exist, and no ViewLimit=0 case. Playbook rule P9: edge cases for changed behaviour.
findings.fix: Add assertions that ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, 99999) returns (false, nil), and that a share created with ViewLimit=0 returns false on its first consume with ViewCount still 0.
findings.verification_note: Traced the scenario against store/db/sqlite/memo_share.go:174-184 and the test at store/test/memo_share_test.go:196-237. The mutants the finding names would not survive the existing test. With `rows >= 0`, the third consume of the exhausted limit-2 share (lines 219-221) affects 0 rows, the mutant returns true, and `require.False(t, ok)` at line 221 fails. Dropping the `view_count < view_limit` guard does the same thing: the third consume would update a row and return true, and line 221 fails. The WHERE clause treats limit 0 the same way as any other limit (`view_count < view_limit`), so a limit-0 share and an exhausted limit-2 share go through the same path. A nonexistent id also gives RowsAffected == 0, the same result line 221 already pins. No plausible mutant of this single conditional UPDATE returns true for an unknown id or a zero limit but false for an exhausted share, so the claim that the test still passes has no concrete wrong outcome behind it. P9 could not be checked: the context pack does not include the playbook section and contains no P9 entry, and its acceptance criteria only require the limit-2, unlimited and list cases, which the test covers. Adding the two extra assertions would be good hygiene, but the failure scenario as written is refuted.

notes:
All three drivers now store view_limit and view_count. Create inserts view_limit when set, and list and get select both columns. ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, id) (bool, error) runs 1 conditional UPDATE ("... SET view_count = view_count + 1 WHERE id = ? AND (view_limit IS NULL OR view_count < view_limit)") and returns true only when exactly 1 row changed. Migrations are store/migration/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/26.10/00__add_memo_share_view_limit.sql, and each driver's LATEST.sql has the same columns. A fresh install now records schema 26.10.1. Two existing tests changed for that: TestFreshInstall now expects 26.10.1, and the calver-newer guardrail case now uses 26.10.2. Test added: TestMemoShareViewLimitConsumption in store/test/memo_share_test.go. `DRIVER=sqlite go test ./store/...` passes. The MySQL and PostgreSQL SQL was not run. In the slice gate, the `prove` step only built the area (nit area.build-only), so it did not run the tests against the pre-change tree. I ran the new test directly and it passes.
